s.q: If a piecewise function is continuous at a point and you must find constants
s.n: Evaluate each side's limit with standard limits/expansions ($\frac{\sin kx}x\to k$, $\frac{\ln(1+x)}x\to1$, rationalise roots). Equate. Two unknowns need two conditions (e.g. continuity at two joins, or continuity + differentiability).

s.q: If it asks the number of points where $f$ is not differentiable (with $|\ |$, $\max$, $\min$)
s.f: |g(x)|\ \text{fails at simple zeros of } g;\ \ \max/\min\ \text{fails at crossings with different slopes}
s.n: Sketch! Mark the corners: zeros of the inside of each modulus, joining points of pieces, crossing points of $\max/\min$. Check each: if slopes differ, count it. A modulus multiplied by a factor that vanishes there is smooth.
s.h: Trap: $|x-1|\sin|x-1|$ is differentiable at $1$ (the factor kills the corner).

s.q: If $[\,]$ (greatest integer) is involved and it asks for discontinuities
s.n: List integer values $g$ passes through in the interval; at a turning point where $g$ only touches an integer from above, there is no jump. Differences like $[\frac{x^2}2]-[\sqrt x]$: jumps may cancel — test both sides.

s.q: If it is a functional equation with differentiability ($f(x+y)=f(x)f(y)$, $f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)+\ldots$)
s.n: Typical results: $f(x)f'(y)+f'(x)f(y)$ gives $f=e^{x/2}$; $f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)+axy$ gives a quadratic.

s.q: If $f$ is defined as a limit ($\lim_{n\to\infty}x^{2n}$ or $x^{2/\theta}$)
s.n: Write $f$ piecewise on $|x|<1$, $|x|>1$, $x=\pm1$, then check continuity at $\pm1$.

s.f: \text{fix the constants from continuity/differentiability first, then do the second part}
